veranderings.rede: 'n regte verskil' calques English 'a real difference'; 'werklike' is the natural Afrikaans word with the same meaning and length.

veranderings.blok: Dinge wat jy elke dag kan doen
veranderings.voor: Maak kompos van skille en blare en spaar water
veranderings.na: Maak kompos van skille en blare, en spaar water
veranderings.rede: Two separate commands are joined by 'en' right after the list 'skille en blare'; the comma separates the two clauses so the child does not read 'spaar water' as a third thing compost is made of.

veranderings.voor: Suid-Afrika hou elke jaar in die eerste week van September Nasionale Boomplantweek.
veranderings.na: Suid-Afrika hou Nasionale Boomplantweek elke jaar in die eerste week van September.
veranderings.rede: The long time phrase in front of the object makes the sentence heavy; naming the week first reads more naturally with the same words.
Afrikaans waters a plant or tree with 'natgooi'; 'natmaak' just means to make wet. The protected 'kan maklik doodgaan' is untouched.

vlae.rede: The block heading still says 'Boomplantdag', while the block itself says the day has become Nasionale Boomplantweek. A heading cannot be changed by the language step; the writer may want the heading and the text to name the same thing.
